newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan opposition denies fall of northeastern town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition denies fall of northeastern town.

text.p: Afghan opposition forces on Wednesday denied a report that they had lost control of the northeastern town of Taloqan, headquarters of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, to the Taleban Islamic militia.

A Pakistan-based Afghan news service said the Taleban had seized Taloqan, capital of Takhar province, with the help of local commanders and local people after an overnight offensive from neighbouring Kunduz province.
Opposition spokesman Dr Abdullah told reporters that the Taleban were nowhere near Taloqan. "Taleban forces are neither in Taloqan nor anywhere else in Takhar province," he said.

He acknowledged that Taleban supporters had entered the Bangi area of Takhar from neighbouring Kunduz province on Tuesday but said they were driven out on Wednesday by the forces of former government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.

Abdullah, speaking by telephone from the opposition-held Panjsher Valley north of Kabul, said Masood's forces had crushed a revolt by a local Pashtun tribe in Takhar and also taken Chardara district in central Kunduz, killing 150 pro-Taleban fighters.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) service quoted unspecified Afghan opposition sources in the Pakistani border town of Peshawar as confirming the fall of Taloqan.
Rabbani and Ittehad-i-Islami faction chief Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf have used Taloqan as a base since the Taleban drove the Rabbani government from Kabul in September.

AIP said the Taleban, who control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, had launched a major offensive into Takhar province from Kunduz on Tuesday evening, killing 20 soldiers loyal to Masood and capturing 285 after intense fighting. The Taleban lost eight dead.
AIP said two helicopters had taken off from Taloqan for an undisclosed destination on Tuesday, apparently with opposition leaders on board, but it could not identify them.
Abdullah said Rabbani had been in the main northern opposition-held town of Mazar-i-Sharif for the past few days.
